content:
The second part of the Goal section is confusing.
"If a character being replaced is not a letter, keep the case of a substitute letter."
In a recent clash, I spent at least 5 minutes trying to understand what is a "substitute letter". I still don't get it. I could get 100% because I was basically trying to "Reverse Mode" it by looking at the inputs and outputs and looking for a pattern until my code passed all test cases.

https://www.codingame.com/clashofcode/clash/report/48791684491ef67e4c00b9da9ccf38f72f3d66a
This contribution hasn’t received enough positive votes from the community. The "REVERSE" option has therefore been deactivated.

Problem description is a little confused. The task is to reverse a string and then it mentions characters to be replaced and substitute letters. This takes  unpleasant amounts of guesswork to figure out.

✅ Approved the contribution.

I thought the same first, but decided to leave the wording as is. To me, the replacing (and the reversing as well) is just an idea, not the directive to actually replace smth in your data structure. This time, after the second thought I may change the first part of the sentence like this "If a character in the original string is not a letter, keep the case of a substitute letter." What do you think?
